findings.issue: When fetch_metrics fails, the new receipt reports MEASURED 0/13 and zero sessions instead of UNAVAILABLE; main does not propagate source availability.

Quota coverage trusts file mtime from scan_quota_snapshots while the UI uses payload updated_at. Copying an old snapshot makes the receipt fresh and the UI stale; the new runtime smoke exercises this contradiction.
A fresh envelope with empty or failed runners counts as quota-observable. The external JSON trust boundary requires a successful runner before asserting coverage.
macOS configuration is read from ~/.config instead of dirs::config_dir()'s ~/Library/Application Support, so normal packaged-app configuration is always unknown.
Historical registered IDs and archived initial scope IDs can be replaced without validation failing; only selected values and array lengths are pinned.
The receipt validator accepts unknown provider IDs, numerators inconsistent with provider_ids, and MEASURED/UNAVAILABLE state contradictions.

needs-human: future baseline versions have no independent immutable reference; after adding a later baseline its scope can be changed again under the same ID/version. The persistence/version approval contract must be chosen before extending the initial pinned history.

summary: Fixed six defects in source availability, quota freshness/runner validation, macOS config lookup, archived-baseline integrity and receipt consistency; reproduced 17 Python and one Node regression failures before the fixes, then passed 126 tests plus registry, inventory and syntax checks. needs-human: choose an immutable reference/approval contract for future baseline versions; OpenAB signal ownership, packaged WebView/runtime acceptance and the synthetic comprehension study remain unverified. Broad suites retain pre-existing chain-staleness/runtime-sync failures, and the worktree sentinel flags unrelated untracked .impeccable/hook.cache.json.
